title: Evaluation of the efficacy of intravenous lidocaine on chronic postoperative pain in patients requiring emergency abdominal surgery. Randomized, double-blind, controlled, multicenter study – LIDOC-POPEYE.
official: Evaluation of the efficacy of intravenous lidocaine on chronic postoperative pain in patients requiring emergency abdominal surgery. Randomized, double-blind, controlled, multicenter study – LIDOC-POPEYE.
summary: Main objective: The primary objective of the study is to demonstrate the efficacy of continuous intravenous lidocaine infusion during emergency abdominal surgery on postoperative complications, 6 months after the procedure.

interventions.name: CHLORURE DE SODIUM PROAMP 0,9 %, solution injectable

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. -Patients aged 18 years or older and under 80 years
2. -Emergency or semi-emergency abdominal surgery of the following types: -urological -gastrointestinal -gynecological
3. -Open or laparoscopic surgery
4. -Estimated duration of surgery ≥ 60 minutes
5. Informed consent for competent patients. Consent from the designated representative, or emergency procedure, followed by obtaining the patient’s consent to continue treatment after surgery
Exclusion criteria:
1. -Use of a regional anesthesia technique via epidural analgesia
2. -Pregnancy or breastfeeding. Women of childbearing age will undergo a pregnancy test prior to enrollment. -Porphyria
3. Porphyria
4. Surgery in Connection with a Transplant
5. - Contraindications to lidocaine: § Known hypersensitivity to lidocaine, excipients, or amide-type local anesthetics. § Complete heart block § Hypovolemia - Contraindications to treatment with 0.9% NaCl: § Hyperchloremia § Hypernatremia § Severe cases of fluid overload and water-sodium retention, particularly in cases of decompensated heart failure, decompensated liver failure (edematous-ascitic cirrhosis), preeclampsia/ eclampsia.
6. - Patients under legal guardianship, conservatorship, or judicial protection.
7. -Uncorrected high-degree atrioventricular block, chronic treatment with Class I antiarrhythmic drugs
8. -Shock defined by a systolic blood pressure ≤ 90 mmHg upon admission to the emergency operating room
9. -Respiratory failure defined by a respiratory rate > 25 breaths/min and/or a pulse oximetry O₂ saturation < 90% upon admission to the emergency operating room
10. -Neurological failure defined by a Glasgow Coma Scale score ≤ 13 upon admission to the emergency operating room
11. Known dementia
12. -Active drug users or those undergoing withdrawal, given the significant challenges in managing perioperative analgesia in these patient
